entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Æthelwold of Winchester (æthelwold-of-winchester) was a pivotal figure in the tenth-century monastic reform movement in Anglo-Saxon England.

As Bishop of Winchester from 963 to 984, Æthelwold played a crucial role in shaping the religious landscape of the region.

He was instrumental in promoting a more austere and ascetic form of Christianity, which emphasized the importance of prayer, fasting, and charitable works.

Æthelwold's reforms had a profound impact on the monasteries of England, leading to a significant increase in the number of monasteries and the quality of monastic life.

The reforms also had far-reaching consequences for the English Church as a whole, contributing to the development of a more centralized and hierarchical structure.

Despite the significance of his reforms, Æthelwold's legacy was largely forgotten until the 20th century, when historians began to reevaluate his importance in the context of Anglo-Saxon England.

"The Church of England would not have been possible without the reforms of Æthelwold of Winchester," notes historian David Walker.

"Æthelwold's vision of a more austere and ascetic Christianity helped to shape the course of English religious history."
